senses.gloss: m. (b. h.) cloud, frequently used in the sense of cover protection.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 60:16">Gen. R. s. 60</cite> <he>כל זמן … היה ע׳ קשור וכ׳</he> as long as Sarah lived, a cloud was tied over the entrance of her tent; <he>וכיון שמתה פסק אותו ע׳</he> and when she was dead, that cloud ceased.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:6:1">Cant. R. to II, 6</cite> <he>וימינו זה עֲנַן שכינה וכ׳</he> … ‘and his right hand embraces me’, that means the cloud of the Divine Presence in the future world (with ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 60:19">Is. LX, 19</cite>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 3:3:5">Y. Taan. III, 66ᶜ</cite>, v. <cite ref="P00984"><he>עָנָיו</he></cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>עֲנָנִים</he>.

<cite ref="Taanit 9b:11">Taan. 9ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 2:6">Gen. II, 6</cite>) <he>מלמד שהע׳ מתגברים וכ׳</he> this teaches that the clouds (like a hose) swell and rise to the sky, and there open their mouth like a hose and receive the rain water; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 13:11">Gen. R. s. 13</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 13:11">Ib.</cite> <he>אין ע׳ אלא מלמעלה</he> clouds (like a hose to receive the waters) come from above (ref. to <cite ref="Daniel 7:13">Dan. VII, 13</cite>); <he>אין ע׳ אלא מלמטה</he> the clouds come from below (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 135:7">Ps. CXXXV, 7</cite>); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 1:5:4">Y. Succ. I, 52ᵇ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 883:7">Yalk. Ps. 883</cite>.

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 3a:1">R. Hash. 3ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 21:1">Num. XXI, 1</cite>) <he>שמע … ונסתלקו עַנְנֵי כבוד</he> he heard that Aaron was dead, and the clouds of glory were removed. Tanḥ. R’eh 16 <he>משיב רוחות ומעלה ע׳ ומוריד וכ׳</he> causes the winds to blow, and the clouds to rise, and the rains to come down; a. fr.
